pr.title: Share the repository inbox by relay location, and let an agent scope an item to one repository
pr.head: f2c018c3ff27499edf90526d2e5d579c249e5c36

summary: Projector lets an agent post a question, request, or notice to another person’s inbox. The preceding layer lets sessions share a relay location: one GitHub repository that carries encrypted records for several work repositories. This layer makes the peer inbox follow that location too, so the same entry can reach sessions working in different repositories.

The sender can restrict an item to one work repository with --repo. Other sessions can still find it with inbox list --relay or the console. Items and replies identify their source repository and its visibility, so a reader can recognize content that crosses a repository boundary.

The exact-head review requests one fix: displaying a sent item embeds reply previews without each reply’s private-source notice. Showing that reply directly includes the notice. The real two-machine rollout check remains deferred until after merge.

cards.title: Terms used below
cards.html:
• Work repository: the repository a session works in.
  • Relay location: the repository carrying encrypted records for those sessions.
  • Mirror: the local numbered inbox entries opened from those encrypted records.
  • Scope: the optional work repository whose sessions should display an incoming item.

cards.title: Validation
cards.html:
• The configured gate passed, including 255 hook tests and the exact-head CI check.
  • The focused peer and relay suites passed 140 tests.
  • A temporary two-machine reproduction confirmed the missing notice on a sent item’s embedded reply.

groups.title: Keep the inbox at the shared location
groups.kicker: Routing and source metadata belong to each record.
intro: A peer inbox entry is an encrypted record addressed to a person’s key. Its mirror now belongs to the relay location instead of the sender’s work repository. Each new item or reply carries the work repository it comes from, while older records without source fields remain accepted.

An incoming item can carry scope_repo, which hides it from ordinary lists in other work repositories. The relay-wide list and console keep those entries visible with a label. Source labels and private-source notices are computed for the repository reading the entry.

files.note: Centralizes source fields and the reminder printed when content leaves a repository that is not public.
Routes posts, responses, lists, and wakeups through the relay location, and renders the sender’s source and optional scope.

checks.text: Showing a sent item checks only that item’s source, then embeds reply previews. A private reply from another work repository therefore appears without its source label or private-source notice. Apply those annotations to each embedded reply before its preview.
The temporary two-machine fixture and focused tests confirm that ordinary lists filter incoming scope while the relay-wide list retains the entry.

groups.title: Use the registration’s location in commands
groups.kicker: CLI and console actions resolve the same inbox.
intro: The registration records both where a session works and where it relays. Inbox commands now use that recorded relay location to find and change numbered entries. Without a session, they resolve the current checkout’s configured location.

Posting refuses a location waiting for consent or one whose relay check refuses it. The CLI adds --relay for the full location inbox and --repo beside --to for an item’s display scope. The console deliberately includes items scoped to other repositories so they remain discoverable.

files.note: Adds scope and relay-wide listing options, resolves location-based mirrors, and passes source fields into replies.
Requests every location entry, including those scoped to another work repository.

groups.title: Watch the location’s mirror in the panel
groups.kicker: The panel follows the same inbox as the CLI.
intro: The Claude Code panel notices new inbox entries by watching a local mirror directory. It now reads the registration’s location to choose that directory, falls back to repo for older registrations, and watches no relay inbox while consent is pending. The regular CLI list still supplies the panel’s filtered rows.

files.note: Resolves a safe relay location from the registration, including legacy and waiting cases.
Watches the relay location’s mirror before refreshing the panel’s inbox rows.

groups.title: Exercise shared and scoped inbox delivery
groups.kicker: Temporary machines verify the visible behavior.
intro: The relay fixtures provide temporary repositories and two simulated machines with different peer keys. New cases send through a shared location, check repository scope and relay-wide discovery, exchange replies, and verify labels and private-source notices. They also cover a checkout with no GitHub origin and reject malformed source metadata.

checks.text: Ran the peer and relay test modules: all 140 tests passed. A separate fixture reproduction confirms the review finding on embedded replies.

groups.title: Explain scope and private-source handling
groups.kicker: Document the commands and record what remains to check.
intro: The command reference and message skill now describe a location-wide peer inbox and how one item can target sessions in a single work repository. They tell an agent to describe private work in general terms before sending it to a peer. The project plan records the implemented decisions and automated acceptance evidence.

checks.text: The outcome marks the implementation complete while deferring the exchange across two real repositories on two machines until after merge.
